title: Food and restaurants
goal: By the end of this lesson you can name Quebec meals and dishes, order politely in a restaurant, ask for the bill, and understand the Quebec meal names déjeuner, dîner and souper.

body: Quebec keeps the older French meal names. In Quebec, *le déjeuner* is breakfast, *le dîner* is lunch, and *le souper* is supper. In France, *le petit-déjeuner* is breakfast, *le déjeuner* is lunch and *le dîner* is supper.
So if a Quebec colleague says *On dîne à midi?*, they mean lunch. The verbs follow the same pattern: *déjeuner* (to have breakfast), *dîner* (to have lunch), *souper* (to have supper).
learn.tip: In Quebec: déjeuner, dîner, souper = morning, noon, evening.

body: Polite ordering uses *je voudrais* (I would like), *je vais prendre* (I'll have), or simply *Pour moi, …* The server may ask *Qu'est-ce que je vous sers?* or *Avez-vous choisi?*

Courses: *l'entrée* (the starter; in North American English 'entrée' means the main course, but in French it is the first course), *le plat principal* (main course), *le dessert*. Drinks are *les boissons*.
Partitive articles are essential here: *du pain*, *de la soupe*, *de l'eau*, *des frites*. After a negative they become *de*: *Je ne veux pas de sel.*

body: To ask for the bill, standard French says *l'addition*; in Quebec you will very often hear *la facture*. Both are understood everywhere in Quebec.
Tipping (*le pourboire*) is expected in Quebec, usually 15 to 20 percent. The server brings the card machine and asks *Ensemble ou séparé?* (Together or separate?).
For takeout, Quebec says *pour emporter*; France usually says *à emporter*. A counter clerk will ask *Pour ici ou pour emporter?*

*La poutine*: fries, cheese curds (*le fromage en grains*) and gravy (*la sauce brune*). *La tourtière*: a meat pie eaten especially at Christmas. *Le pâté chinois*: Quebec's version of shepherd's pie (beef, corn and mashed potatoes).
*La cabane à sucre* (sugar shack) is a spring tradition: you eat ham, beans, pancakes and *la tire sur la neige* (maple taffy on snow), all with maple syrup (*le sirop d'érable*).

quebec.intro: Quebec uses déjeuner, dîner and souper for breakfast, lunch and supper, and has its own food culture: poutine, tourtière, pâté chinois and the spring cabane à sucre.

items.note: Standard in Quebec at every level
A 'dîner' at noon; the 'heure du dîner' is lunch break
Souper is standard Quebec French, not slang
Informal Quebec; liqueur does not mean alcohol here
Very common in Quebec speech: épluchette de blé d'Inde = corn roast

write.prompt: Write a short review (5–6 sentences) of a restaurant you went to: what you ate, how it was, the service and the price.
write.model: Samedi, je suis allé dans un petit resto à Québec. Comme entrée, j'ai pris une soupe à l'oignon. Ensuite, j'ai mangé une tourtière avec des patates. C'était délicieux! Le serveur était très gentil et rapide. Ça a coûté environ trente dollars avec le pourboire. Je vais y retourner.
